A.objective: From authoritative data-room sources only, enumerate represented billed revenue (invoices) that are associated with counterparties whose active contracts contain acquisition-relevant conditions, reporting identifiers and invoice facts as they appear in the sources.

exclusions: expired statements of work treated as inactive contracts
invoices with no path to a contract counterparty unless reported with unresolved association

required_semantic_distinctions.description: A contract is active for this purpose unless it is an expired statement of work. Inactive contracts do not qualify counterparties for exposure.

Contractual term qualifies when it: (1) requires consent or notice on change of control; (2) permits termination upon change of control; or (3) requires consent or notice before assignment, including assignment restricted to affiliates only or assignment prohibited to a competitor.
Each output row links an invoice to a contract_id with association asserted (confident join) or unresolved (cannot confidently associate billed name to contract counterparty).
Invoice records as authored in billing sources, including amount, currency, period, and status fields.
invoice_id, contract_id, and billed_name reported as they appear in authoritative sources (rendering transforms deferred to downstream consumer contracts).

epistemic_requirements: Ground every asserted invoice–contract association in source evidence; do not infer association from name similarity alone.
Missing or uncertain identity between a billed name and a contract counterparty must not be treated as a negative contractual finding.
When association cannot be made confidently, emit the invoice with association unresolved rather than omitting it or asserting a join.
Acquisition-relevant condition presence is a purpose-evaluated judgment over contract text, not a mechanical string match unless sources make the term explicit.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: Invoice is in scope but billed_name cannot be confidently linked to the contract counterparty governing the relationship.

completeness_expectations.row_coverage: Every invoice that qualifies under purpose policies (represented revenue tied to a counterparty with an active contract bearing an acquisition-relevant condition) appears exactly once in invoices.
completeness_expectations.field_coverage: For each included invoice, amount, currency, period, status, billed_name, contract_id, and association are populated.
completeness_expectations.negative_findings: Do not emit rows for invoices that fail purpose inclusion criteria; absence from output is not a closed-world negation of exposure.
completeness_expectations.unresolved_reporting: Invoices blocked only by identity uncertainty are still reported with association unresolved.

purpose_specific_policies.inclusion_rule: Include an invoice when: (1) it is represented billed revenue in sources; (2) it can be associated (asserted or unresolved) with a contract; (3) that contract is active under this purpose's active-contract rule; and (4) the contract contains at least one acquisition-relevant condition.
purpose_specific_policies.active_contract_rule: Expired statement of work is not an active contract.
purpose_specific_policies.association_threshold: Assert association only when evidence supports a confident join between billed name and contract counterparty; otherwise unresolved.
not_world_truth: The label acquisition-relevant and its clause taxonomy are analytical thresholds for purpose A, not independent world propositions.
The active/inactive contract classification for expired SOW applies to this purpose's exposure question, not as a global contract lifecycle fact unless separately grounded in sources.

B.objective: From authoritative data-room sources only, reconcile customer and commercial identities across CRM, billing, company registry, and contracts, reporting whether pairs of records denote the same legal counterparty, are distinct, or remain unresolved.

entities_in_scope: contract parties identified by contract filename

required_output_shape.ordering: sort links by left ascending, then right ascending

required_semantic_distinctions.description: Two referents confidently denote the same legal counterparty.
Two referents confidently denote different legal counterparties.
Insufficient evidence to assert same or distinct; explicit positive unresolved state.
Exact legal-form variants of the same registered name may be treated as mechanical equivalences for SAME_ENTITY.
Distinct registry entities with similar trade names are not automatically the same party.
CRM accounts, billed names, registry rows, and contract filenames as thin referents grounded in sources.

epistemic_requirements: Do not globally merge records merely because two names look similar.
SAME_ENTITY and DISTINCT require establishing evidence, not mere compatibility or absence of contradiction.
Missing a positive same-entity judgment is not a negative (distinct) judgment.
Permit and report explicit UNRESOLVED when confidence is insufficient.
Symmetric presentation: each link is an oriented pair in output but identity judgment is logically symmetric.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: Cannot confidently determine whether left and right referents denote the same legal counterparty.

completeness_expectations.link_coverage: Include every link required to connect a CRM account, its billed name, the contract governing that relationship, and any registry row that is a candidate legal entity for that relationship.
completeness_expectations.pair_granularity: Emit explicit links between identifier-form referents; do not collapse the reconciliation graph without recording intermediate links.
completeness_expectations.negative_findings: DISTINCT is allowed only with grounding; absence of SAME_ENTITY does not imply DISTINCT.
completeness_expectations.ordering: Full link set present; sorted for stable consumption.

purpose_specific_policies.merge_prohibition: No global transitive closure or automatic clustering across all names; judgments are pairwise with stated evidence.
purpose_specific_policies.similarity_threshold: Surface-name similarity alone is insufficient for SAME_ENTITY.
purpose_specific_policies.mechanical_equivalence: Exact legal-form variants of a registered name may be resolved mechanically to SAME_ENTITY.
required_connection_paths: crm account to billing billed name
crm or billing to governing contract
candidate registry entity to commercial relationship records
not_world_truth: Commercial relevance of a name for inclusion is a purpose-scoped selection policy.
The required link set is defined by this purpose's connectivity obligations, not by an exhaustive all-pairs identity matrix over the data room.

C.objective: From authoritative data-room sources only, compute which counterparties are commercially dependent under stated relationship and obligation criteria, using purpose B identifier forms and reporting dependent or unresolved status per active contract.

entities_in_scope: contractual obligation clauses (exclusivity, auto-renewal, rolling term)
universe_scope.identifier_forms: Same as purpose B: crm:, billing:, registry:, contract:

required_output_shape.ordering: sort dependencies by contract_id ascending; obligation_kinds sorted within each row

required_semantic_distinctions.description: Present when there is an open invoice and/or an active contract that auto-renews or continues on a rolling term.
Expired contracts do not create current dependency. One-off paid historical invoice without an active contract does not establish current relationship.
Active contract contains an exclusivity commitment.
Active contract has a rolling term that continues unless notice is given.
Both current commercial relationship and at least one listed obligation kind hold for the counterparty–contract pair.
Dependency evaluation blocked because identity needed to join invoice and contract is unresolved.
Invoice status indicating non-terminal/open state per billing sources.

epistemic_requirements: Commercial dependence is a conjunction of purpose-defined relationship and obligation predicates.
If identity required to join invoice and contract is unresolved, report status unresolved rather than dependent or implicitly false.
Do not treat unresolved identity as evidence of non-dependence.
Obligation kind labels must be drawn only from the allowed enum and grounded in contract text or explicit source fields.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: Cannot evaluate dependence because counterparty identity linking invoices to contracts is unresolved.

completeness_expectations.row_coverage: Emit a dependency row for each counterparty–contract pair that meets inclusion criteria or is blocked solely by unresolved identity required for the join.
completeness_expectations.field_coverage: counterparty, contract_id, open_invoice_ids (possibly empty), obligation_kinds (sorted), and status populated per row.
completeness_expectations.negative_findings: Pairs failing purpose predicates without identity blockage are omitted; omission is not a closed-world negation of dependence.
completeness_expectations.cross_purpose_dependency: Identity judgments consumed from purpose B linkage; unresolved identity propagates to unresolved dependency status.

purpose_specific_policies.dependence_rule: Counterparty is commercially dependent when: (1) current commercial relationship holds, and (2) the active contract contains at least one of exclusivity, auto_renewal, or rolling_term.
purpose_specific_policies.current_relationship_rule: Satisfied by an open invoice OR an active contract with auto-renewal or rolling term continuation.
exclusions: Expired contracts do not create current dependency.
One-off paid historical invoice without an active contract does not establish current relationship.
purpose_specific_policies.identity_join_policy: Use purpose B identifier forms and identity links; unresolved join forces status unresolved.
not_world_truth: Commercial dependence is an analytical composition for purpose C, not a standalone world relation.
Open invoice and active contract thresholds are purpose-scoped predicates that may differ from purpose A active-contract rules.

cross_cutting.source_boundary: Authoritative files in this data room only; downstream world compilation must not require rereading heterogeneous sources.

world_eligible: Source observations: parsed invoice fields, contract text extractions, CRM rows, registry rows.
Thin referents with grounding to source locations.
Mechanical correspondences with deterministic joins (exact IDs, dates, amounts).
purpose_only: Acquisition-relevant condition taxonomy and exposure inclusion (A).
Confidence thresholds and required link sets for identity reconciliation (B).
Commercial dependence composition, current-relationship test, and obligation-kind enum (C).
Output dispositions: association asserted/unresolved, epistemic SAME_ENTITY/DISTINCT/UNRESOLVED, status dependent/unresolved.

kernel_constraints: No new semantic primitives beyond Referent, named typed n-ary Relation, Derivation.
Explicit unresolved state where modeled; no invented closed-world negation.
Purpose outputs under purpose_ir/{a,b,c}/output.json matching visible purpose schemas.
